sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian Languages (revised edition). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: All Siraya mentions checked (±40 lines): historical/classification only; no remark on Siraya stress.

sources.citation: Adelaar, K. Alexander. 1997. Grammar notes on Siraya, an extinct Formosan language. Oceanic Linguistics 36(2): 362-397. doi:10.2307/3622990
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Sections 5.1 Siraya orthography (pp. 366-370) and 5.2 Siraya phonemics (pp. 370-372) read in full: discusses vowel length ('little seems to indicate that vowel length was phonemic in Siraya', p. 367; 'the evidence for phonemic vowel length in Siraya is not strong', p. 368), doubled consonants as a Dutch spelling habit, the diacritics of the sources (apostrophe, dieresis, circumflex, hyphen) and palatalization; no statement about stress or accent anywhere in the article (scanned a full-text search for stress/accent/penult: 0 hits; acute-looking marks in examples are the palatal vowel ä, not st…

sources.citation: Joby, Christopher. 2025. Language revitalisation using historical texts: The case of Siraya. International Journal of Taiwan Studies (advance article), 1-35. doi:10.1163/24688800-20251427 (CC BY 4.0)
sources.note: Section 6.1 'Phonology of Siraya' compares the Dutch-text phonology with revived Siraya (loss of the u/ou short-long distinction, geminates dropped, e vs schwa kept, dieresis for syllable boundaries); nothing about stress or accent (0 hits).

sources.note: Open-access review; short, low chance of a stress remark but cheap to check when the server is up.
